Paper Name: Uncertainty-Aware Dynamic Fusion for Multimodal Clinical Prediction Tasks
Authors: Jiayu Guo, Ying Cheng, Wen He, Yuejie Zhang, Rui Feng, Xiaobo Zhang
Key Idea + Method Used: Proposes Uncertainty-Aware Weighting (UAW) — modality importance is dynamically adjusted based on per-modality reliability/uncertainty at inference time. Coupled with Expert Ensemble Fusion (EEF) using self-attention and modality-specific FFNs to preserve critical cross-modal information. Applied to ICU clinical prediction tasks.
Contribution: First dynamic fusion framework for clinical multimodal data that weights modalities by their uncertainty rather than fixed importance; demonstrates improved accuracy and robustness on phenotype classification and mortality prediction tasks using heterogeneous ICU data.
Research Gap: Does not address small dataset regimes or adversarial content (e.g., memes); uncertainty estimation relies on clinical data distributions and does not extend to vision-language tasks with semantic incongruence.
Relation to Your Work: Directly inspires the uncertainty-aware gating network in AdaptiveFusionModelV3, where per-modality softmax entropy is fed into the gating network alongside CLIP similarity features to produce confidence-aware alpha weights.
Citation: Guo J., Cheng Y., He W., Zhang Y., Feng R., Zhang X. (2024). Uncertainty-Aware Dynamic Fusion for Multimodal Clinical Prediction Tasks. ICASSP 2025, IEEE.

Paper Name: DWCMA: A Vision-Language Fusion Method with Dynamic Weight and Cross-Modal Attention Mechanism
Authors: Jiaqi Li, Hui Gao
Key Idea + Method Used: Introduces Dynamic Weight and Cross-Modal Attention (DWCMA) framework combining: (1) Cross-Modal Attention (CMA) that injects low-level features from one modality into another via attention, and (2) Dynamic Weight (DW) mechanism that adaptively adjusts image vs. text importance based on task demands. Integrated with CLIP for vision-language retrieval.
Contribution: Demonstrates that combining static cross-modal attention with a dynamic weighting module on top of CLIP outperforms single-modal and static-fusion baselines on vision-language retrieval tasks; ablation validates both CMA and DW components independently.
Research Gap: Evaluated on retrieval tasks, not classification of adversarial or hateful content; dynamic weighting is task-level, not sample-level, so it does not adapt per-instance based on modality confidence or semantic incongruence.
Relation to Your Work: Provides conceptual grounding for combining cross-modal attention with dynamic weight allocation — directly reflected in your CrossModalAttentionV2 module and the learned alpha gating over image and text CLIP features.
Citation: Li J., Gao H. (2024). DWCMA: A Vision-Language Fusion Method with Dynamic Weight and Cross-Modal Attention Mechanism. University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, IEEE.

Paper Name: Topology-Aware Dynamic Reweighting for Distribution Shifts on Graph
Authors: Weihuang Zheng, Jiashuo Liu, Jiaxing Li, Jiayun Wu, Peng Cui, Youyong Kong
Key Idea + Method Used: TAR framework dynamically adjusts sample weights during training by propagating gradient flow through graph edges, leveraging inherent graph topology to address OOD distribution shifts in node classification. Avoids strict invariance assumptions of prior methods by providing distributional robustness guarantees theoretically.
Contribution: First method to incorporate graph topology into sample reweighting for OOD generalization; provides theoretical proof of distributional robustness; achieves SOTA on node classification OOD benchmarks (ICML 2025).
Research Gap: Specific to graph-structured data; dynamic reweighting operates on structural topology, not on semantic modality-level signals or per-sample difficulty in multimodal vision-language settings.
Relation to Your Work: Provides theoretical motivation for using dynamic sample reweighting (as opposed to static loss weights) to improve robustness under distributional shifts — analogous to the distributional challenge of hateful vs. benign meme imbalance.
Citation: Zheng W., Liu J., Li J., Wu J., Cui P., Kong Y. (2025). Topology-Aware Dynamic Reweighting for Distribution Shifts on Graph. Proceedings of the 42nd ICML, PMLR 267.

Paper Name: A Dynamic Reweighting Strategy for Fair Federated Learning
Authors: Zhiyuan Zhao, Gauri Joshi
Key Idea + Method Used: DRFL dynamically adjusts per-client aggregation weights on the server side to improve fairness across heterogeneous federated clients. Combines dynamic weight adjustment with a biased client selection strategy. Does not alter local optimizers, only modifies global aggregation.
Contribution: Proposes a server-side fairness-aware dynamic reweighting framework for federated learning that outperforms FedAvg and q-FFL; decouples fairness from local training, making it plug-and-play.
Research Gap: Addresses client-level fairness in distributed learning, not sample-level modality reweighting in a centralized multimodal classifier; no relevance to vision-language or adversarial content tasks.
Relation to Your Work: Provides conceptual background on dynamic reweighting as a principled fairness mechanism — analogous to using alpha to fairly weight underperforming modalities (e.g., image modality on text-only hateful memes).
Citation: Zhao Z., Joshi G. (2022). A Dynamic Reweighting Strategy for Fair Federated Learning. ICASSP 2022, IEEE. Carnegie Mellon University.

Paper Name: A Radar and Camera Cross-Modal Fusion Attention Method for Foreign Object Debris Detection
Authors: Songqi Li, Liangcheng Cai, Peigang Liu, Peng He
Key Idea + Method Used: FFOD-Net uses parallel multi-receptive-field + channel attention for radar and camera feature extraction, followed by cross-modal attention with dynamic feature enhancement and multiscale detection for FOD detection on airport runways (92–94 GHz radar band).
Contribution: Achieves 80.55% mAP@0.5 on a novel self-collected FOD dataset; demonstrates that cross-modal attention with dynamic feature enhancement outperforms simple concatenation/summation fusion; presents end-to-end sensor fusion pipeline for safety-critical deployment (IEEE Sensors Journal 2026).
Research Gap: Domain-specific (radar + camera for object detection); dynamic enhancement is feature-map-level, not a learned scalar gating over modalities; not applicable to text-image semantic fusion for content classification.
Relation to Your Work: Cross-modal attention with dynamic enhancement directly parallels your CrossModalAttentionV2; demonstrates the general principle that learned cross-modal attention outperforms static fusion even for very different modality types.
Citation: Li S., Cai L., Liu P., He P. (2026). A Radar and Camera Cross-Modal Fusion Attention Method for Foreign Object Debris Detection. IEEE Sensors Journal, Vol. 26, No. 4. DOI: 10.1109/JSEN.2026.3652129.

Paper Name: Adaptive Multimodal Fusion: Dynamic Attention Allocation for Intent Recognition (DAF / MVCL-DAF)
Authors: Bo Hu, Kai Zhang, Yanghai Zhang, Yuyang Ye
Key Idea + Method Used: Proposes Dynamic-Attention Allocation Fusion (DAF) with an adaptive network that allocates attention both within modalities and across modalities dynamically per sample. Combines with Multi-View Contrastive Learning (MVCL-DAF) where text acts as primary modality and guides audio/visual modules. Each modality infers intent independently; DAF integrates globally.
Contribution: First method to simultaneously allocate intra- and inter-modal attention dynamically per sample in intent recognition; MVCL component provides contrastive alignment using text as anchor; significantly outperforms SOTA on MIntRec and MIntRec2.0 (AAAI 2025).
Research Gap: Applied to audio-text-vision triplets for intent; contrastive learning uses text as fixed anchor and may not generalise to settings where the image is the primary hate signal; does not handle adversarial image-text incongruence.
Relation to Your Work: The MVCL-DAF contrastive component directly motivates your SupConLoss applied with text and image features as two views. The per-sample dynamic attention allocation mirrors your learned gating network producing sample-wise alpha.
Citation: Hu B., Zhang K., Zhang Y., Ye Y. (2025). Adaptive Multimodal Fusion: Dynamic Attention Allocation for Intent Recognition. AAAI 2025, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence.

Paper Name: Adaptive Cross-Attention Gated Network for Radar-Camera Fusion in BEV Space (ACAGN)
Authors: Ji-Yong Lee, Jae-Hyeok Lee, Dong-oh Kang
Key Idea + Method Used: ACAGN uses deformable cross-attention to align radar and camera BEV features with spatial precision, combined with an adaptive gated network that dynamically filters and prioritises relevant information from each sensor modality. Built on top of RCBEVDet baseline for autonomous driving 3D object detection.
Contribution: Demonstrates that deformable attention + adaptive gating outperforms naive summation/concatenation in radar-camera fusion on nuScenes; improves stability under diverse environmental conditions (ICACT 2025).
Research Gap: Spatial fusion of sensor streams; gating is spatial/channel-level not semantic scalar weighting; no semantic incongruence (modalities are always spatially co-registered), unlike meme text-image pairs.
Relation to Your Work: The adaptive gated network design principle (learn what to pass from each modality rather than statically blend) is architecturally analogous to your DynamicGatingNetworkV3 that outputs alpha based on cross-modal feature descriptors.
Citation: Lee J., Lee J., Kang D. (2025). Adaptive Cross-Attention Gated Network for Radar-Camera Fusion in BEV Space. ICACT 2025, IEEE. ETRI, Republic of Korea.

Paper Name: Dynamic Loss-Based Sample Reweighting for Improved Large Language Model Pretraining
Authors: Daouda A. Sow, Herbert Woisetschläger, Saikiran Bulusu, Shiqiang Wang, Hans-Arno Jacobsen, Yingbin Liang
Key Idea + Method Used: Instance-level dynamic reweighting during LLM pretraining: each training sample's weight is adjusted online based on its current loss value, allowing the model to dynamically prioritise more informative samples. Develops theoretical convergence analysis for loss-based reweighting on gradient optimisation. Validated on 7B and 1.4B parameter LLMs.
Contribution: First formal theoretical characterisation of how loss-based sample reweighting affects convergence bounds in gradient optimisation; achieves faster convergence and improved downstream performance on large LLMs (ICLR 2025).
Research Gap: Applied to text-only LLM pretraining on static datasets; dynamic weighting is loss-magnitude-driven, not confidence- or modality-uncertainty-driven; does not address multimodal fusion or small adversarial datasets.
Relation to Your Work: Theoretical grounding for dynamic per-sample weighting as a training improvement strategy — relevant to the focal loss formulation and R-Drop used in your V3 training to focus learning on harder/more uncertain samples.
Citation: Sow D.A., Woisetschläger H., Bulusu S., Wang S., Jacobsen H., Liang Y. (2025). Dynamic Loss-Based Sample Reweighting for Improved Large Language Model Pretraining. ICLR 2025. arXiv:2502.06733.

Paper Name: DriftShield: Autonomous Fraud Detection via Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning with Dynamic Feature Reweighting
Authors: Jialei Cao, Wenxia Zheng, Yao Ge, Jiyuan Wang
Key Idea + Method Used: Uses Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) reinforcement learning with continuous action spaces to simultaneously optimise detection thresholds and feature importance weights. Dynamic feature reweighting adapts to concept drift; adaptive experience replay with sliding windows + prioritised sampling prevents catastrophic forgetting; entropy-driven exploration balances known/emerging patterns.
Contribution: First application of continuous-action SAC RL to fraud detection; 18% higher detection rate, 57% faster adaptation to concept drift; cumulative detection rate of 0.849 (+7.7% over SOTA) (IEEE Open Journal of Computer Science, 2025).
Research Gap: Sequential financial transaction setting; dynamic reweighting is RL-driven and adapts over time to distributional drift, which is a fundamentally different regime from static multimodal fusion; not applicable to vision-language meme classification.
Relation to Your Work: Entropy-driven exploration and dynamic feature importance weighting conceptually parallels your entropy regularisation on alpha and the dynamic gating mechanism; demonstrates the general value of entropy-based exploration signals in adaptive systems.
Citation: Cao J., Zheng W., Ge Y., Wang J. (2025). DriftShield: Autonomous Fraud Detection via Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning With Dynamic Feature Reweighting. IEEE Open Journal of Computer Science. DOI: 10.1109/OJCS.2025.3587001.

Paper Name: DynCIM: Dynamic Curriculum for Imbalanced Multimodal Learning
Authors: Chengxuan Qian, Kai Han, Jiaxin Liu, Zhenlong Yuan, Zhengzhong Zhu, Jingchao Wang, Chongwen Lyu, Jun Chen, Zhe Liu
Key Idea + Method Used: DynCIM combines: (1) sample-level curriculum based on prediction deviation, consistency, and stability to dynamically assess difficulty; (2) modality-level curriculum measuring global and local modality contributions; (3) gating-based dynamic fusion to adaptively adjust modality weights. Applied to bimodal and trimodal benchmarks.
Contribution: First framework to simultaneously address both sample-level and modality-level imbalance in multimodal learning; consistently outperforms SOTA on 6 benchmarks including Kinetics-Sounds and CMU-MOSEI; demonstrates modality-specific curriculum ordering improves convergence (CVPR-adjacent, 2025).
Research Gap: Curriculum difficulty is computed from prediction deviation — requires warm-up training; does not leverage a pretrained alignment signal (e.g., CLIP cosine similarity) for zero-cost difficulty estimation; tested on balanced task datasets, not adversarially curated hate detection.
Relation to Your Work: Directly inspires curriculum.py — your implementation uses CLIP cosine similarity as a difficulty proxy (low sim = hard adversarial meme) to build a phase-1 easy subset, mirroring DynCIM's sample-level curriculum logic. The gating-based fusion also validates your alpha-based dynamic weighting.
Citation: Qian C., Han K., Liu J., Yuan Z., Zhu Z., Wang J., Lyu C., Chen J., Liu Z. (2025). DynCIM: Dynamic Curriculum for Imbalanced Multimodal Learning. arXiv:2503.06456v3.

Paper Name: DynaFuse: Dynamic Fusion for Resource Efficient Multi-modal Machine Learning Inference
Authors: Hamidreza Alikhani, Anil Kanduri, Pasi Liljeberg, Amir M. Rahmani, Nikil Dutt
Key Idea + Method Used: DynaFuse combines design-time intrinsic value (from training) with run-time extrinsic value (input data quality + sensor energy budgets) to compute updated modality weights at inference. Applied to human activity recognition and stress monitoring with wearable sensor modalities.
Contribution: Achieves up to 22% prediction accuracy gain and 34% average energy savings over static fusion approaches by dynamically deprioritising noisy or low-battery modalities at run time; first framework to jointly optimise accuracy and energy in MMML inference.
Research Gap: Run-time modality quality is defined by sensor noise and battery levels — not by semantic content; no mechanism for cross-modal semantic alignment or adversarial incongruence between modalities; not applicable to text-image classification.
Relation to Your Work: Demonstrates that static modality weight assignment is suboptimal when modality reliability varies per sample — the core motivation for your learned, input-dependent alpha gating in AdaptiveFusionModelV3.
Citation: Alikhani H., Kanduri A., Liljeberg P., Rahmani A.M., Dutt N. (2023). DynaFuse: Dynamic Fusion for Resource Efficient Multi-modal Machine Learning Inference. University of California Irvine / University of Turku, IEEE.

Paper Name: Dynamic Multimodal Fusion (DynMM)
Authors: Zihui Xue, Radu Marculescu
Key Idea + Method Used: DynMM generates data-dependent forward paths during inference via a gating function that makes modality-level or fusion-level on-the-fly decisions. A resource-aware loss encourages computational efficiency. For easy samples, unneeded modality paths are skipped; for hard samples, all paths activate.
Contribution: Proposes a new direction for dynamic multimodal networks; reduces computation by 46.5% on CMU-MOSEI with negligible accuracy loss and improves NYU Depth V2 segmentation with 21% compute savings; demonstrates instance-wise inference is both efficient and expressive.
Research Gap: Gating decisions are coarse (modality-level on/off), not a continuous learned weighting; the resource-aware loss is specific to compute budgets and does not optimise for adversarial or imbalanced classification tasks.
Relation to Your Work: DynMM's core insight — that different inputs require different modality emphasis — is the philosophical foundation of your dynamic alpha gating. Your model extends this to a continuous, differentiable weighting rather than binary on/off gating.
Citation: Xue Z., Marculescu R. (2023). Dynamic Multimodal Fusion. arXiv:2204.00102v2. University of Texas at Austin.

Paper Name: Dynamic Re-weighting for Long-tailed Semi-supervised Learning
Authors: Hanyu Peng, Weiguo Pian, Mingming Sun, Ping Li
Key Idea + Method Used: Extends FixMatch SSL to imbalanced (long-tailed) settings by proposing dynamic re-weighting of unlabeled data based on effective number and temporal variation in pseudo-label counts. The weighting adapts each epoch as pseudo-label distributions shift during training.
Contribution: First SSL method to apply dynamic re-weighting to unlabeled data in long-tailed settings; provides SOTA on CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet127 under various imbalance ratios; demonstrates that dynamic (vs. static) weighting significantly improves minority class accuracy (WACV 2023).
Research Gap: Specific to SSL with pseudo-labels; imbalance is class-level (head vs. tail), not modality-level; not applicable to multimodal fusion or adversarial content detection with a small labelled dataset.
Relation to Your Work: Provides motivation for treating the binary hateful/benign class imbalance in Hateful Memes via dynamic (focal) loss weighting rather than static class weights — conceptually aligned with the adaptive weighting used in your FocalLoss with alpha=0.75.
Citation: Peng H., Pian W., Sun M., Li P. (2023). Dynamic Re-weighting for Long-tailed Semi-supervised Learning. WACV 2023, IEEE. Baidu Research. DOI: 10.1109/WACV56688.2023.00640.

Paper Name: Dynamic Weighted Multimodal Financial Forecasting Models: Fusion Strategies and Market Validation (DWMF)
Authors: Dazhi Yue
Key Idea + Method Used: DWMF uses an attention-based dynamic weight allocation module to quantify real-time contributions from financial modalities (market volatility, investor sentiment, macroeconomic events). GRUs capture cross-modal temporal dependencies; adversarial training enhances robustness. Validated on CSI 300 and S&P 500.
Contribution: Reduces average prediction error by 25.4% and improves Sharpe ratio by 38.5% over static fusion and single-modal baselines; identifies a coupling effect between pricing efficiency and volatility suppression; demonstrates cross-market scalability of the modular dynamic weighting framework.
Research Gap: Financial time-series domain; dynamic weighting is attention-driven at the token/time-step level, not a learned scalar gating over distinct semantic modalities; temporal dynamics do not correspond to the spatial/semantic incongruence challenge in meme content.
Relation to Your Work: Demonstrates the broad applicability of attention-based dynamic weight allocation for multi-modal fusion, validating the general architectural approach; adversarial training for robustness parallels R-Drop regularisation used in your training pipeline.
Citation: Yue D. (2024). Dynamic Weighted Multimodal Financial Forecasting Models: Fusion Strategies and Market Validation. Xiamen Institute of Technology, IEEE.

Paper Name: Dynamical Reweighting for Biased Rare Event Simulations
Authors: Bettina G. Keller, Peter G. Bolhuis
Key Idea + Method Used: Reviews theoretical frameworks for recovering correct molecular dynamics from biased (enhanced-sampling) simulations. Covers two-state, multistate, and path-integral reweighting; connects to transition path sampling; discusses non-equilibrium force reweighting and integration with collective-variable optimisation.
Contribution: Comprehensive review of dynamical reweighting theory for rare event molecular simulations; provides unified framework spanning kinetic models, path integrals, and non-equilibrium settings (Annual Review of Physical Chemistry, 2024).
Research Gap: Physical chemistry / molecular simulation domain — entirely unrelated to machine learning or multimodal classification. The reweighting here refers to statistical mechanics, not loss/sample weighting in neural network training.
Relation to Your Work: Minimal direct relevance; included as contextual background for the general concept of 'dynamical reweighting' across scientific domains. The notion of correcting for distributional bias via reweighting is philosophically analogous to focal loss and class-imbalance reweighting in your system.
Citation: Keller B.G., Bolhuis P.G. (2024). Dynamical Reweighting for Biased Rare Event Simulations. Annual Review of Physical Chemistry, 75:137–162. DOI: 10.1146/annurev-physchem-083122-124538.

Paper Name: Family Space Dynamic Reweighting for Malware Classification (FSDR)
Authors: Zisen Qi, Binbin Li, Tianning Zang, Xingbang Tan
Key Idea + Method Used: FSDR estimates the 'spanned space' (feature-space coverage) of each malware family by treating samples as identically distributed random variables and analysing their correlations. A non-parametric formula derives a weighting scheme inversely proportional to family spanned space; weights adapt as features evolve during training. Applied on Malimg and MaleVis datasets.
Contribution: Introduces spanned-space as a better proxy for class representation than sample count alone; dynamic reweighting outperforms static class-frequency weighting for long-tailed malware classification; demonstrates code-available reproducibility.
Research Gap: Unimodal image classification task (malware visualisation); dynamic reweighting is class-level (family-level), not sample-level or modality-level; no cross-modal interaction or adversarial content considerations.
Relation to Your Work: Provides supplementary motivation for dynamic class reweighting in imbalanced settings; parallels the use of focal loss with class-imbalance handling in your pipeline for the hateful (minority) vs. benign (majority) meme distribution.
Citation: Qi Z., Li B., Zang T., Tan X. (2024). Family Space Dynamic Reweighting for Malware Classification. Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences, IEEE.

Paper Name: Multimodal Dynamics: Dynamical Fusion for Trustworthy Multimodal Classification
Authors: Zongbo Han, Fan Yang, Junzhou Huang, Changqing Zhang, Jianhua Yao
Key Idea + Method Used: Proposes Multimodal Dynamics: sparse gating captures within-modality feature informativeness; true class probability measures modality-level classification confidence; a transparent fusion algorithm integrates modalities based on dynamically estimated informativeness. Designed for safety-critical applications (medical multiomics). CVPR 2022.
Contribution: First work to jointly model both feature-level and modality-level informativeness variation for trustworthy multimodal classification; improves both accuracy and trustworthiness (stability + explainability) on medical multimodal datasets over SOTA.
Research Gap: Medical multiomics domain; trustworthiness is framed around feature-noise and missing-modality scenarios in clinical data, not adversarial image-text mismatch; class probability-based confidence requires reliable per-modality classifiers which may not exist in zero-shot CLIP settings.
Relation to Your Work: The sparse gating over modality-level confidence directly inspired the auxiliary head design in your model (img_aux_head, txt_aux_head) — their softmax entropy feeds into the gating network as uncertainty signals, extending this paper's confidence-based informativeness to your uncertainty-aware alpha computation.
Citation: Han Z., Yang F., Huang J., Zhang C., Yao J. (2022). Multimodal Dynamics: Dynamical Fusion for Trustworthy Multimodal Classification. CVPR 2022, IEEE. Tianjin University / Tencent AI Lab.

Paper Name: Learning to Optimize Multi-Objective Alignment Through Dynamic Reward Weighting
Authors: Yining Lu, Zilong Wang, Shiyang Li, Xin Liu, Changlong Yu, Qingyu Yin, Zhan Shi, Zixuan Zhang, Meng Jiang
Key Idea + Method Used: Introduces dynamic reward weighting for multi-objective online RL alignment of LLMs. Two approaches: (1) hypervolume-guided weight adaptation that maximises objective space coverage; (2) gradient-based weight optimisation. Continuously adjusts reward weights during training to explore Pareto fronts, avoiding fixed-weight linear scalarisation failures.
Contribution: Addresses the theoretical failure of fixed-weight linear scalarisation for non-convex Pareto fronts; achieves Pareto-dominant solutions with fewer training steps on multiple LLM alignment benchmarks; compatible with PPO, GRPO and other RL algorithms (TACL 2026).
Research Gap: LLM alignment via RL; dynamic weighting is over reward objectives (accuracy vs. length vs. clarity), not over input modalities in a fusion system; no relevance to multimodal hate detection.
Relation to Your Work: The principle of dynamically weighting multiple training objectives parallels your compound loss (focal + R-Drop + aux + SupCon + entropy + diversity) — each term is a 'reward signal' whose weight is manually set but could be dynamically tuned using gradient-based methods like those proposed here.
Citation: Lu Y., Wang Z., Li S., Liu X., Yu C., Yin Q., Shi Z., Zhang Z., Jiang M. (2026). Learning to Optimize Multi-Objective Alignment Through Dynamic Reward Weighting. TACL 2026. University of Notre Dame / Amazon.

Paper Name: Long-Tailed Image Recognition with Dynamic Re-Weighting (DRHT)
Authors: Xinyuan Li, Yu Wang, Jien Kato
Key Idea + Method Used: Proposes Dynamic Re-Weighting (DR) where category weights follow a progress-relevant schedule: weight first increases then decreases proportionally to how many samples have been seen per category. Combines with Head-to-Tail (HT) loss that gradually transfers model attention from head to tail categories. Validated on long-tailed CIFAR and ImageNet.
Contribution: Demonstrates that progress-relevant (non-monotonic) dynamic weighting outperforms both static reweighting and monotonic inverse-frequency weighting; improves tail accuracy without sacrificing head accuracy; generic weight assignment compatible with any long-tail loss function.
Research Gap: Unimodal image classification; class-level reweighting for long-tailed distributions, not modality-level or cross-modal reweighting; progress-relevant schedule assumes clear head/tail distinction, which does not map directly to binary hate/benign classification.
Relation to Your Work: Conceptually supports the use of dynamic (focal) loss weighting rather than static class weights for the imbalanced Hateful Memes dataset; the idea of gradually shifting model focus motivates curriculum learning (curriculum.py) from easy to hard adversarial samples.
Citation: Li X., Wang Y., Kato J. (2023). Long-Tailed Image Recognition with Dynamic Re-Weighting. ICASSP 2023, IEEE. Ritsumeikan University / Hitotsubashi University.

Paper Name: MixFEAN: Enhancing Multi-Object Tracking for Intelligent Sports Analysis through Conditional Feature Mixing and Dynamic Re-weighting
Authors: Zhihao Zhang, Chen Zhang, Wenyue Liu, Wan Ahmad Munsif Bin Wan Pa, Nur Shakila Binti Mazalan
Key Idea + Method Used: MixFEAN combines: (1) FcMixup — feature-level conditional mixing of the most similar feature representations to improve model adaptability; (2) Feature Decoupling Re-weighting Module (FDRM) that dynamically adjusts feature map weights to focus on key targets. Applied to multi-object tracking in sports (LSP, SportsMOT datasets).
Contribution: Improves MOT accuracy by 1.1% on LSP and significantly on SportsMOT; demonstrates that embedding-space MixUp enhances robustness to motion variability; FDRM dynamic re-weighting improves anti-jamming capability in complex sports environments.
Research Gap: Multi-object tracking in video; MixUp is applied between visually similar features (nearest-neighbour mixing), not between semantically incongruent modalities; no text modality or adversarial semantic content.
Relation to Your Work: FcMixup directly motivates the feature-level MixUp implemented in your _dynamic_step: mixing CLIP embeddings (img_feat, txt_feat) in embedding space after extraction, before fusion — the same principle of operating in feature space rather than input space to preserve semantics.
Citation: Zhang Z., Zhang C., Liu W., Wan Pa W.A.M., Mazalan N.S. (2024). MixFEAN: Enhancing Multi-Object Tracking for Intelligent Sports Analysis through Conditional Feature Mixing and Dynamic Re-weighting. National University of Malaysia, IEEE.

Paper Name: Multimodal Dual Cross-Attention Fusion Strategy for Autonomous Garbage Classification System (MDCF)
Authors: Huxiu Xu, Wei Tang, Zhaoyang Li, Kecheng Qin, Jun Zou
Key Idea + Method Used: MDCF fuses image and impact-sound modalities using dual cross-attention that captures both intramodal and intermodal relationships. Deployed in a physical garbage classification device. Accounts for homogeneity limitations between image and audio by using bidirectional cross-attention.
Contribution: Proposes dual (bidirectional) cross-attention for multimodal fusion; achieves high recognition rate with low processing time on a self-built multimodal garbage dataset; demonstrates industrial-grade deployment in a physical classification system (IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics, 2024).
Research Gap: Image + audio fusion for physical object classification; dual cross-attention is bidirectional but does not include dynamic scalar gating between modalities; no text modality, no adversarial semantic incongruence between modalities.
Relation to Your Work: Bidirectional cross-attention design validates your CrossModalAttentionV2 which applies cross-attention in both directions (image attending to text features and vice versa); confirms that capturing intermodal relationships via attention outperforms simple concatenation.
Citation: Xu H., Tang W., Li Z., Qin K., Zou J. (2024). Multimodal Dual Cross-Attention Fusion Strategy for Autonomous Garbage Classification System. IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics, Vol. 20, No. 11. DOI: 10.1109/TII.2024.3435508.

Paper Name: Multimodal Emotion Analysis Based on Multi-Scale Feature Fusion and Cross-Modal Attention: Architecture Comparison and Feature Extractor Optimization
Authors: Siyuan Xu
Key Idea + Method Used: Proposes a framework integrating multi-scale features (hierarchical feature extraction at multiple depths) with cross-modal attention for multimodal emotion/sentiment analysis. Systematically compares 5 fusion architectures (CMAC, OTE, HSTEC, NaiveCat, NaiveCombine) and multiple feature extractors (InceptionV3, WideResNet50, MobileNetV2, ResNet50/101, BERT/RoBERTa). CMAC framework uses adaptive weight allocation.
Contribution: Provides comprehensive empirical benchmark of fusion architectures and extractors for multimodal sentiment analysis; identifies BERT+WideResNet50 as optimal balance; confirms CMAC with adaptive weight allocation significantly outperforms naive fusion; validates channel attention for text feature extraction (ICAITA 2025).
Research Gap: Sentiment analysis domain; multi-scale extraction is evaluated at different ResNet/InceptionV3 layers, not CLIP ViT layers; adaptive weight allocation in CMAC is architecture-level, not a per-sample learned scalar gating with uncertainty signals.
Relation to Your Work: Directly motivates the multi-scale CLIP feature extraction improvement suggested in your literature survey (extracting from layers -4, -2, -1 of ViT); confirms that adaptive weight allocation improves over static fusion baselines, supporting the core thesis of your dynamic vs. static model comparison.
Citation: Xu S. (2025). Multimodal Emotion Analysis Based on Multi-Scale Feature Fusion and Cross-Modal Attention: Architecture Comparison and Feature Extractor Optimization. Communication University of China, ICAITA 2025.
